newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT, GAS OIL DIPS IN LETHARGIC TRADE.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT, GAS OIL DIPS IN LETHARGIC TRADE.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures lost some ground in early listless trade on Wednesday following slightly bearish overnight U.S. statistics, brokers said.
"There's nothing happening, look at the volumes. It's just sitting there. The only people who are phoning are journalists," one said.

September Brent traded at 0930 GMT down 12 cents at $18.73 a barrel. Under 1000 lots had moved. September gas oil wasn't faring much better with the last deal done 25 cents off the settle at $170.50 a tonne and just over 100 lots traded.
Weekly U.S. stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute saw a build of over 2.7 million barrels on crude stocks for the week to August 8, against an expected draw of 1.75 million barrels.
"But the runs are down so that is a bit product supportive," another broker said refering to a drop of 2.1 per cent on refinery utilisation over the same period.
News that the first tanker to lift Iraqi oil under the second term of the oil-for-food deal had been delayed was slightly supportive, they said.
Turkey's Ceyhan oil terminal officials said on Wednesday that the tanker had not yet begun loadings and was waiting off the port.

"It's supportive but not really seen as a big deal. We need some strong news to get this market rolling and neither the API's or the Iraqi loading delays are anywhere near strong enough to do that, so we just sit and wait," another broker said.
